clue.text: Who's piece of music in France creates very little commotion

parts.note: qui is the French word for who; 'in France' at the end of the phrase covers both French words
étude is the French word for a study, a short piece of music written to practise technique

explanation.surface: A puzzled listener wonders whose French composition is making so little fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are French words: QUI (who) and ETUDE (a study in music), with 'in France' applying to the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the noun means a state of calm and quiet, which is what you have when there is very little commotion.

clue.text: Loudly advertise second-class anti-flood construction

parts.note: B is the grade below A, so second-class
Noah's ark was built to survive the Flood

explanation.surface: A shoddy flood barrier is being promoted with plenty of noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to shout out a sales pitch, as a fairground barker does, means to advertise loudly.

clue.text: Tanker's workers get tax threshold removed

definitions.note: read as the plural noun tankers: ships that carry oil

indicators.note: removed tells us to take the following letter out of the word for workers

parts.note: toilers are people who labour hard

indicators.note: the threshold of a word is its doorstep, its first letter, here of tax

explanation.surface: The crew of an oil tanker get relief from paying tax on their lowest earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanker's workers' looks like one phrase for the definition, but the definition is only 'Tanker's', read as a plural; 'workers' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense: an oil-carrying ship is also called an oiler, so tankers are oilers.

clue.text: Get free international support

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, is the international body
a stick supports a walker or a plant

explanation.surface: An appeal to win release with help from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to come loose or release something that was jammed is to get it free.

clue.text: Loathsome herbal tea served up — not right!

indicators.note: served up suggests the letters are dished out in a fresh arrangement
not right means the letter standing for right is taken out of the drink

explanation.surface: A disgusted drinker sends back a herbal infusion that is simply wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' removes R from HERBALTEA, leaving HEBALTEA, which 'served up' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something that deserves to be detested or hated is loathsome.

clue.text: Order for stone coffin someone from the West Midlands once executed

parts.note: a cist is a prehistoric stone burial chest

indicators.note: executed means beheaded here, so the first letter is cut off

parts.words: someone from the West Midlands once
parts.note: Mercia was the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the Midlands, so its people were Mercians

explanation.surface: A historical execution order calls for a stone coffin for a Midlander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' takes the head off MERCIAN, leaving ERCIAN. Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Cistercians are a Catholic monastic order of monks and nuns.

clue.text: Room to go forward rapidly without second in command

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the lunge goes around the letter

parts.note: to lunge is to thrust suddenly forward

indicators.note: second in means the second letter of the following word, command

explanation.surface: Instructions to advance quickly when there is no deputy to lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second in command' looks like a deputy, but it means the second letter of 'command', O, which sits inside LUNGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a sitting room or living room in a house is called a lounge.

clue.text: Change amount, it is put about

indicators.note: put about, like a ship turning, signals that the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter a sum and spread the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an alteration in form, especially a genetic one, is a change.

clue.text: SF writer acts like one with film that is withdrawn

parts.note: as in 'he acts as host' means acts like
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: withdrawn means the letters for 'that is' are taken out of the word for film

parts.note: a movie is a film
ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A science-fiction author behaves like someone whose film was pulled from release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' removes IE from MOVIE, leaving MOV.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Isaac Asimov wrote the Foundation and robot novels, classics of science fiction.

clue.text: Quick move made to get cured meat

definitions.meaning: a sudden sharp tug or twitch
meat marinated in spices and grilled, or dried strips like jerky

explanation.surface: Someone moves sharply to grab some preserved meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a sudden jolt, and the Caribbean spiced style of cooked or dried meat, as in Jamaican chicken.

clue.text: Begging that rage in tent be modified

indicators.note: be modified asks for the letters of the phrase before it to be altered into another order

explanation.surface: Pleading that fury inside a tent be toned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: pleading earnestly with someone is begging them.

clue.text: Saps providing supporting directions to such as the Missouri

indicators.note: supporting means holding up, so the directions wrap around and carry the ship

parts.note: W, E and S are compass directions: west, east and south
USS (United States Ship) is the prefix of US Navy vessels such as the battleship Missouri

explanation.surface: Weaklings are giving directions to a river or a battleship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Missouri' suggests the river or the state, but it is the American battleship; 'supporting' has the compass points hold it up on both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: saps and wimps are feeble, timid people, informally called by this slang word.

clue.text: Real loss of work at showroom

indicators.note: work as an instruction to work the letters, kneading them into a new order

explanation.surface: A real job loss at a car showroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the retail area where goods are displayed for customers is a showroom.

clue.text: Celebrity fringes at congress after the end of December can be a net attraction

indicators.note: after places the word for congress behind the closing letters of the month
fringes are the edges, so the outer letters of celebrity

parts.note: the closing three letters of the month's name December
congress here means sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: A celebrity hanging round a year-end conference is drawing the crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of December' gives its last three letters, BER.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: online erotic encounters are an attraction found on the internet, the net.

clue.text: Enthusiasts confined in the bronze age a great deal

parts.note: the run of letters held inside the words bronze age, across the join
lots means a great deal

explanation.surface: Fanatics were kept captive through much of the Bronze Age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Bronze Age' looks like a period; the letters ZEA lie within 'bronze age'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: fanatical devotees of a cause are enthusiasts taken to extremes.

clue.text: Estate residents a number one gets to irritate

parts.note: ten is a number
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
to try someone, as in trying their patience, is to irritate them

explanation.surface: Someone on an estate gets on the nerves of their neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: A collective noun: the body of tenants living on an estate are its residents.

clue.text: Composer, otherwise disrespectable, gets rid of tattered carpets

indicators.note: otherwise asks for the letters of the long word to be arranged differently, once the carpets are taken away

explanation.surface: A rude composer clears out his worn-out rugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets rid of tattered carpets' removes the letters of CARPETS from DISRESPECTABLE, leaving DISEBLE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Léo Delibes was the French composer of the ballet Coppélia and the opera Lakmé.

clue.text: Former visit a total mix-up — one needed to leave?

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: total mix-up says the letters of the following words are thoroughly jumbled

explanation.surface: A previous trip was chaos, so someone needs to get out.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a permit to depart a country, required by some states, is what one needs to leave.

clue.text: Jelly eating out requires plate

indicators.note: requires is read as takes in, so the jumbled word holds the plate letter
out means the letters of eating are put out of their usual order

parts.note: an L-plate is the sign on a learner driver's car in Britain

explanation.surface: Eating jelly out needs a plate to serve it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EATING; 'requires' puts L inside. L-plates are the L signs British learner drivers must display.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance: the clear gelling agent made from animal collagen is used to set a jelly, and is itself a jelly.

clue.text: Unconfined uneasiness resolved after a fashion

indicators.note: resolved, as in broken down into parts, signals the remaining letters are rearranged
unconfined means without its boundary letters, so uneasiness loses its first and last

explanation.surface: Free-floating anxiety is somewhat settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unconfined' strips the ends of UNEASINESS to give NEASINES, which 'resolved' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: both phrases mean partly, in some way or to a limited degree.

clue.text: Managed to get back six grand to Norwegian port

indicators.note: get back means the word for managed is read backwards

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
VI is the Roman numeral for six
K, short for kilo or thousand, is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Someone manages to recover six thousand on the way to a Norwegian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get back' turns RAN into NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Narvik is an ice-free port in northern Norway, scene of battles in 1940.

clue.text: Non-illuminated bend up front leads to the opposite

definitions.note: the opposite of the clue's first word, so meaning brightly lit

indicators.note: up front puts the bend letter at the start of the dark word

parts.note: an S-bend is a bend shaped like the letter S
unlit means not illuminated

explanation.surface: A dark curve in the road where headlights help.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'the opposite' of 'Non-illuminated': putting S in front of UNLIT turns dark into lit by the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym: bathed in daylight is the opposite of non-illuminated.

clue.text: Needed pole to be replaced in a selected position

indicators.note: to be replaced says one pole, north, is swapped for the other, south, within needed

explanation.surface: A post had to be swapped out where it was chosen to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pole' supplies both N (north) and S (south): swap N for S in NEEDED.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports sense: a player placed in a tournament draw so top players avoid each other early is put in a selected position.

clue.text: Lengthen publicity by circular letter on short London opening

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, the publicity trade
O is the letter shaped like a circle
LON is an abbreviation of London
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A circular letter announces an extension to a London opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circular letter' looks like a mailshot; it is O, the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to extend in time or length, an old form of prolong, is to lengthen.

clue.text: Architectural feature providing detailed protection from the elements

indicators.note: detailed read as de-tailed: the last letter is docked

parts.note: cover is shelter from wind and rain

explanation.surface: A building detail described as shielding from the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed, removing the R from COVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a concave moulding where a wall meets a ceiling is an architectural feature.

clue.text: Man's junior partner (so-called) involved in technical fraud

definitions.note: the small island lying just off the southern tip of the Isle of Man

indicators.note: involved in shows the letters are wrapped up within the words technical fraud

explanation.surface: A man's junior colleague is caught up in a technical swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man. The Calf of Man is the islet off its southern tip, its so-called young one, as a calf is to a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A place name: the islet next to the Isle of Man is called the Calf of Man, like a young animal beside its mother.

clue.text: Scaffolder reported stiffness

indicators.note: reported means the word for the worker is heard rather than written

parts.note: a rigger erects scaffolding or ships' rigging

explanation.surface: A scaffolder said to be stiff after a day on site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' signals a homophone: in British speech RIGGER and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: rigidity, as in rigor mortis, is stiffness.

clue.text: Impracticality of one changing lead is beginning to manifest

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of lead swap places to form a new word
beginning to picks out the first letter of manifest

explanation.surface: Someone impractical keeps shifting the lead, and it begins to show.
explanation.definitionFit: A near-synonym: pursuing perfect principles over workable reality is a kind of impracticality.
